sentences.text: This petition under section 482 of Cr.P.C. is filed to quash and set aside FIR being C.R.No.11192010210224 of 2021 registered with Bagodara Police Station, Ahmedabad for the offence under sections 376(2)(n), 384 and 506(2) of IPC.

2. Heard learned advocates for the parties.
3.

Seeking quashment of FIR, learned advocate for the applicant would submit that prosecutrix and applicant were in deep love and relationship since more than 5 years and thereafter, since the relationship became sour, the prosecutrix has filed complaint for the offence of rape in questioned FIR.
It is submitted that sole reason for filing questioned FIR is that marriage between applicant and prosecutrix could not be solemnized.

It is submitted that applicant and prosecutrix who Amitbhai Ishwarbhai Solanki vs State Of Gujarat on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167996151/

Learned advocate for the applicant submitted that applicant and first informant used to celebrate multiple occasion including birth date of first informant.
In nutshell, it is submitted that FIR is filed with mala fide intention and deserves to be quashed.
It is submitted that since relationship of applicant and first informant became sour and inflamed FIR is filed.

It is submitted that continuous of FIR would be absurd process and therefore, the applicant seeks to quash questioned FIR.
4.
Per contra, learned advocate for the first informant objected to grant of relief on the ground that first informant is Anaganwadi Worker since 2015 and married to Gunvantbhai Jadav on 05.05.2009.
It is submitted that out of marriage, prosecutrix has given birth to child.

It is submitted that prosecutrix was in love relationship with applicant till 2007 and since love relationship of petitioner and prosecutrix did not materialized in marriage, prosecutrix ended the relationship.

Learned advocate for the prosecutrix having referred to statement of prosecutrix made in the FIR would submit that thereafter, the applicant was entering into physical relationship with prosecutrix without her consent, under duress and pressure.
It is submitted that applicant was coercing prosecutrix to enter into physical relationship and passing threat.
It is submitted that even applicant has taken financial advance of the victim and she was duped.

Looking to all this facts and NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/16018/2021 ORDER DATED: 12/03/2025 undefined circumstances, more particularly, when victim herself made statement that the applicant has entered into physical relationship without her consent, prima facie, FIR may not be quashed on the belief that applicant and victim were in relationship.
Therefore, it is submitted to dismiss the application.
5. Learned APP submitted that victim in the FIR states that applicant has physically exploited without her consent and rest of the statement made by the applicant can be tested during trial.
In this circumstances, it is submitted to dismiss the application.

It was also urged that investigation is complete, charge is framed and at that time, the applicant has not raised any hue and cry and at present, the Sessions Case is pending for recording of evidence of prosecutrix before the learned Sessions Court.

It is submitted that since material is available against the applicant to put in trial,
further proceeding of FIR cannot be scuttle.
6. I have heard learned advocates for the parties, also perused the record.
By order dated 03.03.2025, this Court has called status report of trial.
Learned Sessions Judge through learned PDJ forwarded report dated 10.03.2025 and it is taken on record.
According to report forwarded by learned Sessions Court, after framing of charge, the matter is at the stage of cross examination.
The report indicates that without any challgenge, the accused has allowed to frame charge and claimed to be tried by denying the charge of rape levelled against him.

In the FIR she has stated that she was kept under threat and coercion to have physical exploitation.

It is stated by prosecutrix that time and again accused who is married person physically exploited her and also Amitbhai Ishwarbhai Solanki vs State Of Gujarat on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167996151/

sentences.text: Therefore, when the investigation by the police is in progress, the court should not go into the merits of the allegations in the FIR.
Police must be permitted to complete the investigation.
It would be premature to pronounce the conclusion based on hazy facts that the complaint/FIR does not deserve to be investigated or that it amounts to abuse of process of law.

During or after investigation, if the investigating officer finds that there is no substance in the application made by the complainant, the investigating officer may file an appropriate report/summary before the learned Magistrate NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/16018/2021 ORDER DATED: 12/03/2025 undefined which may be considered by the learned Magistrate in accordance with the known procedure; Cr.P.C. is very wide, but conferment of wide power requires the court to be cautious.
It casts an onerous and more diligent duty on the court;

xiv) However, at the same time, the court, if it thinks fit, regard being had to the parameters of quashing and the self-restraint imposed by law, more particularly the parameters laid down by this Court in the cases of R.P. Kapur (supra) and Bhajan Lal (supra), has the jurisdiction to quash the FIR/ complaint; and xv) When a prayer for quashing the FIR is made by the alleged accused, the court when it exercises the power under Section 482 Cr.P.C., only has to consider whether or not the allegations in the FIR disclose the commission of a cognizable offence and is not required to consider on merits whether the allegations make out a cognizable offence or not and the court has to permit the investigating agency/police to investigate the allegations in the FIR."

sentences.text: In dealing with the last category, it is important to bear in mind the distinction between a case where there is no legal evidence or where there is evidence which is clearly inconsistent with the accusations made, and a case where there is legal evidence which, on appreciation, may or may NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/16018/2021 ORDER DATED: 12/03/2025 undefined not support the accusations.

When exercising jurisdiction under Section 482 of the Code, the High Court would not ordinarily embark upon an enquiry whether the evidence in question is reliable or not or whether on a reasonable appreciation of it accusation would not be sustained.
That is the function of the trial Judge.
Judicial process, no doubt should not be an instrument of oppression, or, needless harassment.

Court should be circumspect and judicious in exercising discretion and should take all relevant facts and circumstances into consideration before issuing process, lest it would be an instrument in the hands of a private complainant to unleash vendetta to harass any person needlessly.
At the same time the section is not an instrument handed over to an accused to short- circuit a prosecution and bring about its sudden death......................."
(Emphasis supplied)"

10. Applying ratio stated herein above and coming back to the case on hand, FIR discloses offence of rape has been registered by the victim herself and in her statement, she has categorically stated that how she was subjected to physical exploitation under threat.
11.
It is well settled that prosecutrix of sex offence is not an accomplice but a competent witness.

Ordinarily her evidence must carry the same weight as it attached to on injured person, unless there are special circumstances which call for greater caution, it would be safe to act on her testimony if there is independent evidence lending assurance to her accusation.
Ordinarily the evidence of a prosecutrix who does not lack understanding must be accepted, unless she has a strong motive to falsely involve the person charged.

Ordinarily an Indian woman would be most reluctant to lvel false accusation of rape invovling her own reputation unless she has a very strong NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/16018/2021 ORDER DATED:
12/03/2025 undefined bias or reason to do so.
[see State v/s. Chandra Prakash (1990) 1 SCC 550].
12. In the present case, prosecutrix in her statement made accusation on accused for threatening her and what could be noticed that she is married lady.
According to this Court, at this stage, FIR cannot be quashed.

13. In the case of Manik B v/s. Kadapaia Sreyes Reddy [ 2023 (o) JX (SC) 1297], Hon'ble Apex Court in para 3 to 7 has held and observed as under :-
"3. The factors which the Court is required to take into consideration, while quashing the proceedings under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (in short "Cr.P.C.") and while considering an application for discharge

sentences.text: The least we can say is that the High Court in the impugned order, while exercising jurisdiction under Section 482 Cr.P.C., has almost conducted a mini trial and quashed the proceedings.

5. Learned Single Judge of the High Court has elaborately discussed the statements of the witnesses recorded under Section 161 of the Cr.P.C.
6.

Whether the testimony of the witnesses is trustworthy or not has to be found out from the examination-in-chief and the cross-examination of the witnesses when they stand in the box at the stage of such trial.

7. Such an exercise, in our considered view, is not permissible while exercising the jurisdiction under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
8.
The scope of interference, while quashing the proceedings under Section 482 Cr.P.C. and that too for a serious offence like Section 302 of Indian Penal Code is very limited.

The Court would exercise its power to quash NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/16018/2021 ORDER DATED: 12/03/2025 undefined the proceedings only if it finds that taking the case at its face value, no case is made out at all.

9. At the stage of deciding an application under Section 482 Cr.P.C., it is not permissible for the High Court to go into the correctness or otherwise of the material placed by the prosecution in the chargesheet.
The High Court by the impugned order has done exactly the same."
14. In offence of rape, it is argued that FIR is filed belatedly and therefore, FIR should not be believed as true version of victim.
In this regard, no straitjacket formula can be laid down.
In case of sexual offence, the criteria may be different altogether.
As honour of the family is involved, its members have to decide whether to take the matter to the Court or not.
In such fact situation, near relations of the prosecutirx may take time as to what course of action should be adopted.

In the case of Sri Narayan Saha v/s. State of Tirupra [2005) SCC (Cri.) 410], the Hon'ble Apex Court has held as under :
"In India if the prosecutrix happened to be a married person, she will not do anything without informing her husband.

sentences.text: Merely because the complaint was lodged less than promptly, does not raise the question that the complaint was false.
The reluctance to go to the police is becuase of society's attitude towards such women.
It casts doubt and shame upon her rather than comfort and sympathy.
Thefore, the delay in lodging complaint in such cases does not necessarily incidate that her version is false."
15. In the present case, charge is framed.
The case is at the stage of cross examination of prosecutrix.

Therefore, on all above grounds, it is hard to believe that FIR is end relationship of NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/16018/2021 ORDER DATED: 12/03/2025 undefined applicant and prosecutrix and required to be quashed.

17. Before parting with the order, let me refer to report forwarded by learned Additional Sessions Judge, Dholkat dated 10.03.2025.
This Court by order dated 03.03.2025 called report of progress of trial.
Learned Sessions Judge has forwarded report of trial along with some internal written communication exchanged between him and concerned learned JMFC.
The approach of learned Sessions Judge to incorporate such communication in progress report is uncalled for.
There was no reason for learned Sessions Judge to incorporate such communication in progress report of trial.
It is internal correspondence between learned Sessions Judge and learned JMFC.
The Court fails to understand why such communication has been incorporated in the report.
Simply, learned Sessions Judge could have forwarded report that charge in the Sessions Case is framed and stage of trial is at cross examination of prosecutrix.
It could be said that learned Sessions Judge has exceeded his jurisdiction.
Perhaps, learned Sessions Judge intend to communicate that statement of the victim under section 164 of Cr.P.C. is missing.
To be noted that learned Sessions Judge or its office was expected to verify all the papers of Sessions Case when it was committed and send to trial before Sessions Court.
It seems that no such verification is carried by learned Sessions Court or its office.

Communication which took NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/16018/2021 ORDER DATED:
12/03/2025 undefined place between learned Sessions Judge and learned JMFC perhaps is with a view to unshoulder liability of missing statement of prosecutrix / victim under section 164 of Cr.P.C.
Such approach is unacceptable.
Be that as it may.
Learned Principal District Judge concerned is requested to conduct inquiry in regard to missing statement of prosecutrix / victim under section 164 of Cr.P.C. and to do needful for regular trial.
